case_scope: Subsystem case: local land-use democracy, incumbent homeowner veto, and entry closure

democratic_nondomination_gate.note: Local process can look democratic while excluding future residents, renters, workers, and lower-wealth entrants most affected by housing shortage and place access.

local_land_use_veto.note: Housing elements, zoning, permitting timelines, CEQA/litigation, and local hearing participation remain conversion points from existing housing wealth into scarcity protection.

homeowner_outsider_exclusion.note: Incumbent homeowners have stronger standing, turnout, and process access than outsiders who would benefit from entry into opportunity-rich places.

renter_and_future_resident_voice.note: The cube still needs renter/future-resident participation and outcome data to test whether local democracy includes absent claimants.

housing_land_washout.note: Supply restrictions and process delay can wash out wage gains through rent, commuting, crowding, displacement, and inability to enter high-opportunity places.

public_deliberation_voice_equality.note: Supply skepticism can preserve opposition even when voters want affordability; deliberation design matters.

gate_12_democratic_non_domination.why: Gate 12 is blocked because local democratic forms can operate as incumbent-asset veto unless renter, worker, future-resident, and lower-wealth entry claims are represented and converted.

gate_15_place_public_finance.why: Place wealth cannot pass while zoning/permitting processes preserve high-opportunity scarcity and push infrastructure, transport, and housing costs onto excluded households.
